User requirement:
Contract Lifecycle Access

These are the only permissions for users to execute, review, or sign contracts; each permission requires all conditions stated for that activity, based on current recorded facts. Users may hold multiple roles. These permissions neither change contract states nor require an order of activities. Amounts in the supplied records are stored in whole US cents.

A user with the contract administrator role may execute a contract only when its value is at least $0.00, its status is signed, and the request is on the corporate network. If its value exceeds $100,000.00, the host application must also confirm completion of the additional review.

A user with the reviewer role may review a contract only when its value is at least $0.00 and its status is draft. If its value exceeds $100,000.00, the reviewer must not be the contract's drafter.

A user with the signatory or contract administrator role may sign a contract only when its value is at least $0.00, both the user's signing authority and the contract's required authority are levels 0, 1, or 2, and the user's authority is at least the required authority. The user must have used multi-factor authentication, and the contract's counterparty must not be among the user's conflicted counterparties.

Candidate policy:
permit (principal is User, action == Action::"executeContract", resource is Contract)
when { (((resource.contractValue >= 0)) && ((principal.roles.contains(Role::"ContractAdmin"))) && (!(true) || (resource.status == ContractStatusValue::"signed")) && (!((resource.contractValue > 10000000)) || context.executeContractV8ReviewCompleted) && (context.onCorpNetwork)) };

permit (principal is User, action == Action::"reviewContract", resource is Contract)
when { (((resource.contractValue >= 0)) && ((principal.roles.contains(Role::"Reviewer"))) && (!(((resource.contractValue > 10000000))) || (principal != resource.drafter)) && (!(true) || (resource.status == ContractStatusValue::"draft"))) };

permit (principal is User, action == Action::"signContract", resource is Contract)
when { ((((principal.signingAuthority == 0) || (principal.signingAuthority == 1) || (principal.signingAuthority == 2)) && (resource.contractValue >= 0) && ((resource.requiredAuthority == 0) || (resource.requiredAuthority == 1) || (resource.requiredAuthority == 2))) && ((principal.roles.contains(Role::"Signatory") || principal.roles.contains(Role::"ContractAdmin"))) && (!(true) || (principal.signingAuthority >= resource.requiredAuthority)) && (context.mfaUsed) && (!(principal.conflictedCounterparties.contains(resource.counterparty)))) };

Return only JSON with keys approve (boolean) and reason (string). Reject a policy if it is too broad or too restrictive. Treat the code as a single Cedar permit policy; no other permits exist. Do not assume omitted conditions are enforced elsewhere.

User requirement:
Sending Device Commands

A user may send a command to a device only if the user holds at least one of the operator, technician, or fleet administrator roles, the device is active, and its firmware tags include “stable”. The request’s current time must be at or after its scheduled start time and strictly before its scheduled end time. Times are in UTC. The request’s source IP address must be within 10.0.0.0/8.

If the device is in maintenance mode, the maintenance command must also be authorized. This additional requirement applies only while maintenance mode is enabled; all other requirements still apply.

These are the only permissions: sending a device command is allowed when all applicable requirements above are met, and no other actions are permitted.

Candidate policy:
permit (principal is User, action == Action::"sendCommand", resource is Device)
when { (true && ((principal.roles.contains(Role::"Operator") || principal.roles.contains(Role::"Technician") || principal.roles.contains(Role::"FleetAdmin"))) && ((resource.status == DeviceStatusValue::"active")) && (((context.sendCommandScheduledStart <= context.currentTime) && (context.currentTime < context.sendCommandScheduledEnd))) && (!((resource.maintenanceMode == true)) || context.maintenanceCommandAuthorized) && (resource.firmwareTags.contains("stable")) && (context.sourceIp.isInRange(ip("10.0.0.0/8")))) };

User requirement:
Escrow Clear-to-Close Approval

A user may approve an escrow file as clear to close only if the user holds the title officer or escrow manager role and the file’s region is the same group as, or a descendant of, the user’s assigned group.

The file must have funded status, a held amount of at least $0.00, a payee count of at least zero, and cleared title. Its lien status must not contain “tax_lien”. The request’s current time must be on or before the file’s closing date, with times evaluated in UTC. Amounts in the supplied records are stored in whole US cents.

These are the only permissions: approval is permitted if and only if all of these requirements are met, and no other activity is authorized by this requirement.

Candidate policy:
permit (principal is User, action == Action::"approveClearToClose", resource is EscrowFile)
when { (((resource.heldAmount >= 0) && (resource.payeeCount >= 0)) && ((principal.roles.contains(Role::"TitleOfficer") || principal.roles.contains(Role::"EscrowManager"))) && (!(true) || (resource.status == EscrowFileStatusValue::"funded")) && ((context.currentTime <= resource.closingDate)) && ((resource.titleCleared == true)) && (!(resource.lienStatus.contains("tax_lien"))) && ((resource.region in principal.assignedGroup))) };
